record.title: Project discovery can lead hooks to read state.json without a file-type or size bound
record.description: `findStateFiles` accepts the first existing `.stilo/state.json` path, and `readStateResult` reads it synchronously without checking its type or size. A symlink to a device or a FIFO could therefore make a hook block or consume memory, depending on platform and filesystem behavior. The source path is present, but this run did not execute it or establish the resulting resource impact or host timeout behavior.
record.claimed_root_cause: `findStateFiles` uses `fs.existsSync`, which follows symlinks and does not restrict the target type. `resolveProjeto` passes the discovered path to `readStateResult`, which calls unbounded `fs.readFileSync`. No regular-file or size check occurs on this wired path. The separate diagnostics reader checks `isFile()`, but it is not called here.

trace.description: UserPromptSubmit resolves project state for the host-supplied cwd. SessionStart and SubagentStart also call project resolution.
`fs.existsSync` accepts an existing state path without checking whether it is a regular file or symlink.
The discovered state path is passed directly to `readStateResult`.
The path is read synchronously with `fs.readFileSync` without a type or size bound.

evidence.description: Discovery checks existence only; no `lstat`, no-follow open, or regular-file check is performed.
The wired state reader calls `fs.readFileSync` without a byte limit.
The UserPromptSubmit path resolves project state before writing hook output.
The prompt reader schedules an unreferenced timer, but synchronous work blocks the event loop while it is running.
The UserPromptSubmit hook declares a five-second host timeout; its process-kill behavior was not observed.
A separate diagnostics reader checks `statSync().isFile()`, but this check is not present in the wired state reader.

blockers: This host has no OS-enforced sandbox, so a symlink-to-device or FIFO fixture was not run. Node behavior, peak memory use, and blocking behavior for these inputs remain unobserved.
Claude Code and Codex host timeout behavior is not visible in repository source; it is unknown whether the hook process is terminated and whether the prompt continues.
Symlink materialization and FIFO availability depend on platform and filesystem configuration; the default Windows checkout may not reproduce the POSIX cases.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated Linux VM with networking disabled, a read-only target, an empty allowlisted environment, a 256 MB memory limit, and a six-second process-group timeout, create a disposable project with a valid local state file replaced in separate runs by a symlink to `/dev/zero` and by a FIFO. Call `resolveProjeto` against that fixture and record exit status, peak memory, and whether it returns before the timeout. Do not run the check if any stated isolation or resource limit is unavailable.
validation_plan.deployment: In a disposable Linux VM with a strict memory cap and process-group timeout, install the plugin in a throwaway Claude Code or Codex profile and open a project containing the same harmless fixtures. Observe whether the host terminates the hook process, whether any child survives, and whether the prompt continues. Do not use a production profile, project, or sensitive data.
